claims.text: Under service-like high-shear and high-strain-rate loading, an initially single-phase high-entropy alloy becomes brittle through in situ grain-boundary decohesion.
The proposed brittle behavior does not require pre-existing grain-boundary segregation or intermetallic precipitation.
CoCrFeMnNi can be prepared as a single-phase solid solution suitable for the proposed initial state.
The proposed initial specimens have a homogeneous microstructure without significant grain-boundary segregation or intermetallic precipitates.
High strain rate or low temperature produces localized shear stress at grain boundaries.
Dynamic nanoclusters may form at grain boundaries or adjacent shear zones during loading.
Transient amorphization may occur at grain boundaries or adjacent shear zones during loading.
Cavitation or nanovoid formation may occur dynamically at grain boundaries under loading.
Shear-induced grain-boundary structural rearrangements momentarily reduce grain-boundary cohesive strength.
Localized grain-boundary decohesion causes early crack nucleation and brittle fracture.
Dynamic boundary changes will become observable after a critical load or strain rate is reached and will precede brittle crack propagation.
Conventional-alloy brittle behavior is preceded by observable segregation and intergranular precipitation.
The same high-entropy alloy remains ductile and shows no significant grain-boundary decohesion under moderate loading.
The proposed mechanism applies chiefly at high strain rates or low temperatures and may not apply during quasi-static or high-temperature deformation.
A moderate-loading specimen of the same alloy and conventional alloys with segregation-associated failure provide controls for the proposed comparison.
Failure to observe a grain-boundary transformation before brittle failure, or observation only of conventional segregation or precipitation, would falsify the proposed dynamic-decohesion mechanism.
